description.narrative: The development objective of Pathways to Sustainable Livelihoods Project for Lesotho is to improve the efficiency and equity of selected social assistance programs and to strengthen the livelihoods of poor and vulnerable households. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Strengthening livelihoods with economic and social inclusion activities, has the following sub-components: (i) Economic inclusion activities and referral services; and (ii) Disability inclusiveness. 2) The second component, Contingency finance for shock-responsive social assistance, provides contingency financing to enable the efficient delivery of emergency cash transfers during a crisis. 3) The third component, Developing equitable and efficient social assistance delivery systems, will strengthen delivery systems with an emphasis on improving equity. 4) The fourth component, Project management, monitoring and evaluation (M&E) and capacity building, aims to strengthen institutional capacity of the Ministry of Social Development (MoSD), which is the implementing agency for project interventions.
To improve the efficiency and equity of selected social assistance programs and to strengthen the livelihoods of poor and vulnerable households

title.narrative: Share of PA households who have had their PA eligibility recertified based on new NISSA data

comment.narrative: The indicator measures the share of PA beneficiaries who have had a new NISSA score calculated based on newly collected NISSA data (urban data collected 2020-21, and rural data collected from 2022 and later) in the NISSA and who have been assessed as being eligible for receiving PA benefits. All others should be exited from the program. As the target, we estimate that 50% those who receive PA benefits at that time, have had their program eligibility confirmed using the NISSA and that all of those who receive payments ae poor or ultra poor according to the NISSA classification (have a score below the NISSA cut off score for PA eligibility). For the urban NISSA data collected in 2020-2021, the ministry has recently made progress in accessing the data and will soon apply the proxy means test (PMT) to all households. During the MTR, it was agreed to hire a firm to conduct data collection across the target 32 community councils, with work expected to commence in April 2025.

title.narrative: Share of rural community councils with updated information in NISSA

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the share of the total 64 rural community councils where the NISSA updating exercise has been implemented and for which new data have been entered into the NISSA system. Household listing and Community based Categorization (the first step of NISSA data collection) has been completed in 17 CCs out of the target of 20 CCs. This represents 78.6 percent of target households (111,765). Enumeration (the second step of data collection and quality control) has been completed in 10 CCs (Tenesolo, Likila, Mphokojoane, Manonyane, Makhoarane, Litsoetse, Lilala, Likolobeng, Seate, and Nqoe) and represent 40.9 percent of target households. In April 2026, data collection was paused due to initiation of the National Census data collection, which will end on May 30, 2026. The firm expects to complete enumeration in the remaining ten CCs across Mafeteng, Mohale's Hoek, Leribe, and Berea district, within 52 days of the start of enumeration, by August 14, 2026

title.narrative: Number of households receiving emergency cash transfers during an eligible emergency, shock, or crisis, including climate shocks

comment.narrative: This indicator is only measured if there is an emergency for which component 2 is used to respond. This indicator is cumulative and adds the number of beneficiaries (individual for individual programs and households for households targeted programs) who have received emergency cash transfer payments over the duration of the project. The eligible shocks would also include climate shocks. In the previous ISR, it was reported that 80,135 beneficiaries received top-up emergency cash transfers during the emergency response (44,502 CGP beneficiaries in 2023 and 44,502 in 2024). However, since this indicator should only count unique beneficiaries, the correct figure is 45,000.

comment.narrative: As of May 2026, 78.9% of OAP beneficiaries are receiving their payments through mobile wallets, surpassing the end target of 60% set for June 2027. This result reflects the successful completion of the digital payments rollout across all the 10 districts of Lesotho, underpinned by a continued data collection drive undertaken by the Ministry. The Ministry will undertake a rapid user experience assessment by June 30 2026, which will inform plans for further digitization of OAP.

title.narrative: Share of CGP payees who have national ID numbers in MoSD system
Share of CGP payees who have national ID numbers in MoSD system

comment.narrative: This indicator measures whether an Application Programming Interface (API) has been built and is active between NISSA and NICR so that the Ministry can verify the ID number of the Ministry social grant program beneficiaries upon enrollment and exit. As of May 2026, 72% of CGP payees have national ID numbers recorded in the Ministry's MISSA system, up from 67% reported in the previous ISR. This reflects sustained progress in the completion of a data matching exercise between MISSA and NICR.

title.narrative: Unit cost (administrative overhead) of payment delivery of the OAP program

comment.narrative: This indicator calculates the unit cost of the administrative overheads associated with delivering payments for the OAP program. The baseline of 5.60% reflects the cost of cash-based payment delivery using payment officers in early 2022, calculated as a percentage of the monthly OAP grant per beneficiary (LSL 1000). The end target of 2.70% is estimated for digital payment delivery via M-Pesa (Vodacom), calculated on the assumption that the OAP benefit will reach LSL 972 in year 5. The unit cost will be updated once the share of digital OAP payments reaches at least 10%, to enable a representative weighted average cost calculation. Currently, 78.9% of OAP payments are being made digitally.

Tertiary bursary program uses NISSA to select beneficiaries

comment.narrative: This indicator measures whether the tertiary bursary program has introduced and is actively using a methodology to identify students from lower income households drawing from the NISSA database to improve the targeting of bursaries for students from lower income households. The Means Testing Bill was retracted from parliament by the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning for review since it had taken a long time to pass through the parliament. The review of the Lesotho National Tertiary Education Student Fund which is aimed at reforming the entire Tertiary Education Fund is still ongoing. Once completed, anticipated to be at the end of June 2024, all relevant stakeholders will be invited to revalidate the policy which informs the bill. These drafts of the Bill and the Policy are intended to adopt and legalize the newly method of means testing for the government scholarship beneficiaries.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of social safety net programs

comment.narrative: Progress has been made in digitizing OAP, reaching 78.9% completion. The CGP target was met through emergency transfers under vertical expansion. While PA has a caseload of 15,996. Public Assistance and Disability Grant digitization rates have increased from zero to 16.5% and 24.2%. Recertification of PA and CGP will commence once NISSA updating has been completed. The Ministry will prepare a plan to replace PA and CGP beneficiaries who are no longer eligible for receiving these benefits, and replacement with eligible individuals on the waiting lists or in NISSA. Kindly note that there was an error in estimating this indicator in November 2025 but has been rectified in this ISR. The November 2025 indicator should have reported 228,545 instead of 301,325.

comment.narrative: The actual current value of 9,213 beneficiaries have received economic inclusion interventions up from 2,220 reported in the previous ISR as of May 2026. This figure reflects an increase of 2,701 beneficiaries who have completed personal initiative training in five community councils in cohort 2 of Lot 1. Additionally, 4,292 beneficiaries have completed at least ten out of twelve sessions of PIT across five community councils in Lot 2. Progress reflects the rollout of cohort 2 of Lot 1 in five community councils during November 2025, and a rollout of Lot 2 in additional five community councils during January 2026 .
